introTitle: Welcome to the AI Exposure Scan!
introBody: This tool is aimed to help you reconsider the assessment structure of your course. To get started, fill out your course name and faculty, and then select your forms of assessment. The exposure score dynamically updates based on your changes, so feel free to play around with it. Keep in mind that this score should be considered an indication. Your work is automatically stored in your browser.
migrationBody: The AI Exposure Scan is now available at https://ai-tlc.github.io/uva-assessment/. Please use the new site from now on. If you have already started working here, save your result before leaving.

s.f.a.denbroeder@uva.nl
compensableNo: A non-compensable in-person exam means students must demonstrate their knowledge in a controlled, AI-free setting regardless of other grades. This significantly strengthens the overall AI resilience of the course. If other assessment is AI sensitive or relates to other learning goals, consider making these products 'build towards' the skills or knowledge tested on the in-person exam to encourage learning.
compensableYes: A compensable in-person exam still carries no AI exposure itself, but students can offset a poor result with other (potentially high-exposure) assessments. The course-level protection is therefore lower.
msgCompensableYes: Your in-person exam is compensable. It carries no AI exposure itself, but students can offset a poor result with grades from higher-exposure components. Consider making it non-compensable for stronger course-level protection.
msgCompensableNull: You have an in-person exam — please indicate above whether it is compensable to get accurate course-level feedback.
intermediateYes: An intermediate product or check-in can give you useful insight into student progress and thinking, but it does not insulate against AI use. Students can still use AI at any stage of the process.
intermediateNo: Without an intermediate product or conversation, you have limited visibility into the process. If time and course structure allow, adding one could give you more information and control over how students approach the work.
inclassYes: An in-class peer review component significantly reduces AI exposure, as students must engage with and evaluate each other's work in a supervised setting.
inclassNo: Without an in-class component, peer review is done at home and students can use AI to write their feedback. Consider adding a brief in-class discussion or defence to verify authentic engagement.
qaYes: A mandatory Q&A or interactive element significantly reduces AI exposure, as students must demonstrate live mastery of their topic. Ensure questions are not superficial to be able to verify if students truly understand the subject.
qaNo: Without a Q&A or interactive element, students can rely heavily on AI-prepared content. If space and time is available, consider adding this element to the assignment.
oralYes: An oral defence reduces AI exposure somewhat, as students must demonstrate live mastery of their work. Ensure questions go beyond surface level to verify whether students truly understand the content.
oralNo: Without an oral defence, students can rely fully on AI to draft or (re)write their text. If space and time allow, consider adding a brief oral check to this assignment.
reflectionYes: An individual reflection component helps verify personal engagement, making it harder for students to rely entirely on AI or other group members. It does not reduce AI exposure, however, as the group work and the reflection can still be AI-assisted, but may add a layer of accountability.
reflectionNo: Without an individual reflection, it is difficult to verify each student's personal contribution and understanding. Consider adding one to strengthen accountability.
full_overviewYes: Having a clear, uninterrupted overview of students and their screens as they conduct the exam can reduce AI exposure, though this kind of invigilation can be very intensive and may not be fool-proof. Consider conducting the exam with UvA-controlled devices, or in handwritten format, to further reduce AI exposure.
full_overviewNo: Without an uninterrupted overview of students and their screens, it is still possible for them to access AI tools during the exam. Consider conducting the exam with UvA-controlled devices, or in handwritten format, to reduce AI exposure.
byodNull: You have an in-person exam on students' own devices — please indicate above whether you have a full overview of students and their screens to get accurate course-level feedback.
avvYes: This assessment does not contribute to the final grade. It therefore does not impact the course's AI exposure, but still carries its own exposure level.
verdictDescLowMustPass: Your course includes a non-compensable in-person exam. Students must demonstrate their knowledge in a controlled setting, making AI-assisted passing of the course very difficult regardless of other components.
verdictDescLow: Your course is well-protected against AI misuse. Students are primarily assessed through methods that are difficult to outsource to AI.
verdictDescMed: Your course has a mixed profile. Some components are exposed to AI use, while others are well-insulated. Depending on your aims, you might want to consider whether high-exposure assessments can be partially replaced or complemented with lower-exposure formats, or if you can skew the weights of your assessment towards low-exposure options.
verdictDescHigh: A large share of your grade is assigned through assessments that students can easily complete using AI tools. Consider redesigning the assessment structure and adapting the weights of your assessment.
msgWeightsOver: Your components currently sum to {total}%. Reduce some weights.
msgWeightsUnder: Your components currently sum to {total}%. You have {remaining}% unassigned.
msgMustPass: Regardless of other components, students must pass your exam in a controlled, AI-free environment in order to pass the course. This substantially lowers the overall AI exposure of the course, but do keep learning goals in mind that are not tested by this exam.
msgHighOver60: {pct}% of the grade comes from high-exposure assessments. Students could potentially complete the majority of this course using AI tools.
msgHighOver40: {pct}% of the grade is high-exposure. Consider shifting some weight to in-person or oral formats.
msgNoLow: You have no low/no-exposure assessments. Adding an in-person exam, oral exam, in-class activity, or graded participation can significantly improve AI resilience.
msgGroupWork: Group work contains high AI exposure because AI contributions are hard to attribute or detect. An intermediate product, individual reflection, or oral defence component can help mitigate this, but do not eliminate the possibility that students use AI.
msgPeerReviewNull: You have a peer review — please indicate above whether it includes an in-class component to get accurate course-level feedback.
msgTakeHomeExam: A take-home exam is unsupervised, so students can use AI to answer or check questions, even under time limits. Therefore, this is not a recommended format. Consider offering an in-person exam or other format instead.
msgTakeHomeMC: A take-home multiple-choice exam is unsupervised, and AI can very quickly suggest or verify answers for most questions. This can also occur when using specific course content. Therefore, this is not a recommended format. Consider offering an in-person exam or other format instead.
msgPresentation: Presentations are medium-exposure: AI can help prepare slides and scripts, but a live interactive element or Q&A can substantially reduce that risk. Use the toggle above to indicate whether your presentation includes one.
msgOralExam: Oral exams are one of the most AI-resilient formats available, but may introduce other biases. Also ensure that students are challenged with difficult questions to prove their mastery of the topic.
msgGroupWorkNull: You have a group project — please indicate above whether it includes an intermediate product/check-in, an individual reflection, and/or an oral defence.
msgTakeHomeNull: You have a take-home assignment — please indicate above whether it includes an intermediate product/check-in and an oral defence.
msgCreativeNull: You have a creative work assignment — please indicate above whether it includes an intermediate product/check-in and an oral component.
helpExposureIntro: The tool assigns each assessment component a default exposure level (high, medium, or low) based on how exposed the assessment type is to AI use. Below, you can see how the main formats are classified. The overall score is a weighted average of the exposure levels, and serves as a broad indication rather than a precise measure.
help_creative-work: Students can use AI to generate (most of) their creative work (for instance, scripts for podcasts and videos), but they cannot outsource everything. Intermediate products and oral components increase visibility of their process, but do not remove the underlying exposure of this format.
help_take-home-writing: Students complete this assignment at home and can easily use AI to draft or (re)write their text, or otherwise complete the assignment. This makes it a high-exposure format.
help_take-home-exam: A take-home exam is unsupervised, so students can use AI to answer or check questions, even under time limits.
help_take-home-mc: For multiple-choice exams at home, AI can very quickly suggest or verify answers for most questions. This can also occur when using specific course content, as these can be uploaded by the student.
help_in-person-byod: The exam is on campus, but students use their own devices. If device and network access are not strictly controlled, AI use remains possible.
help_group-work: Students can use AI to generate (most of) their assignments, and it is difficult to attribute contributions to individual students. Intermediate products and individual reflections increase visibility of their process, but do not remove the underlying exposure of this format.
help_peer-review: During peer reviews, students may use AI to suggest feedback. An in-class peer review component reduces AI exposure by requiring live, supervised engagement.
help_presentation: Presentations are classified as medium-exposure, since AI can help prepare slides and scripts, but students must still present and respond live. A mandatory Q&A or interactive element further reduces the exposure level of this assessment type.
help_in-person-exam: This exam takes place in a supervised, controlled setting where AI use is not possible. Therefore, there is no AI exposure.
help_oral-exam: In oral exams, students must respond to your questions in real time, and you can adapt questions based on their answers. While students can use AI to prepare for this exam, an oral exam mitigates this by asking challenging questions.
help_participation: Graded participation is based on observed engagement and contributions in class, leaving little room for AI to replace student effort.
help_in-class-activity: In-person activities are carried out under supervision, for instance during teaching hours; students might prepare using AI, but the assessed work happens live.
